parts.gloss: will surely do (auxiliary verb of certainty)

literal: If laziness dwells in one's noble family, it will surely thrust one into slavery to one's own enemies.
translation: If laziness takes root in a person of noble birth, it will drag them down and force them into servitude under their enemies.
modern: சோம்பல் ஒருவனுடைய உயர்ந்த குடும்பப் பெருமையில் வந்து தங்கிவிட்டால், அது அவனை அவனுடைய பகைவர்களிடம் அடிமையாகச் சேர்த்துவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet warns of the devastating impact of laziness on a person's social standing. Even if someone is born into an illustrious or noble family (குடிமை), allowing laziness (மடிமை) to dwell within them will destroy their status. It strips away their independence and eventually forces them into a state of servitude (அடிமை) to their adversaries (ஒன்னார்). The poet emphasizes that sloth is not just a passive flaw, but an active force that actively drives a person to ruin.
